data.name: Meta_LanguageName
data.comment: This language's name in itself, shown in the Options dropdown. A language picker names each language the way its own speakers write it, so this is the one key a translator writes in their own language rather than translating: Deutsch, not German.

data.name: Meta_ShippedLanguages
data.comment: Every language tag this build ships, comma separated, English first. Adding a language means dropping in Strings.<tag>.resx and adding its tag here - the whole of it. Read from this file only, never from a translation, so translating this key cannot change what the app offers. A tag with no resources behind it is dropped at startup, which is how qps-ploc can sit here permanently and still only appear in a build made with -p:PseudoLocale=true.

data.name: Options_Language_Description
data.value: The language this app's own text is read in. System default follows the display language Windows is set to. Mod names, descriptions and changelogs come from the Forge and stay in whatever language their author wrote them in.

data.name: Options_Language_SystemDefaultFormat
data.comment: {0} is the language following Windows currently lands on, named in itself - "System default (English)".

data.name: Common_ClearFilters
data.comment: Button label, on both Browse and Installed. Each page explains its own in a tooltip.

data.name: Common_SaveAsDefault
data.comment: Button label, on both Browse and Installed.

data.name: Common_Previous
data.comment: Pager button, on both Browse and Installed. The previous page of results.

data.name: Common_Next
data.comment: Pager button, on both Browse and Installed.

data.name: Common_PinnedToolTip

data.comment: On the pin icon. Four copies of this sentence across Browse and Installed's three views.

data.name: Common_DownloadsFormat

data.name: Common_Close

data.name: Addons_InstalledFormat

data.name: Installed_CategoryFilterToolTip

data.name: Installed_SelectAllToolTip

data.name: Installed_UpdateSelectedToolTip

data.name: ModLists_CaptureDescription

data.name: ModLists_NamePlaceholder

data.name: ModLists_Capture

data.name: ModLists_ImportToolTip
data.value: Open a mod list someone shared with you

data.name: ModLists_SavedEmpty
data.value: Nothing saved yet. Capture what you have installed, or import a list someone sent you.

data.name: ModLists_ServingBadge
data.comment: Badge on the list this machine serves to clients. Short: it sits in a small chip.

data.name: ModLists_ServingToolTip
data.value: This machine serves this list to clients that connect to it. Editing and saving it republishes what they see.

data.name: ModLists_FromServerBadge
data.comment: Badge on a list a server handed to this install.

data.name: ModLists_FromServerToolTip
data.value: A server handed this list to you. It stays exactly as that server wrote it - make a copy to change what's on it.

data.name: ModLists_FollowingServerToolTip
data.value: This install is following this server's list, alongside its own

data.name: ModLists_FollowingToolTip
data.value: This install is following this list

data.name: ModLists_UndoToolTip
data.value: Puts every mod back the way it was before that list was applied. Usually just moves mods - nothing to download.

data.name: ModLists_EmptyState
data.value:
Pick a list on the left, or capture what you have installed now.
A mod list records which mods to install and enable. Applying one downloads whatever is missing from sp-mod.com and sets aside anything the list doesn't name - it never deletes a mod.
data.comment: Shown in the right pane when no list is selected. The blank line between the two paragraphs is deliberate.

data.name: ModLists_PreviewToolTip
data.value: Work out what applying this list would do. Nothing moves and nothing downloads.

data.name: ModLists_ApplyToolTip
data.value: Download what's missing, enable what the list names, and set aside what it doesn't.

data.name: ModLists_BackToModsToolTip
data.value: Stop showing the plan and go back to what this list names. Changes nothing.

data.name: ModLists_ExportToolTip
data.value: Save this list to a file you can send to someone. It carries which mods and versions - never the mod files themselves.

data.name: ModLists_RefreshFromServerToolTip
data.value: Asks the server for this list again, even if its revision hasn't moved - which is what an operator editing and republishing the list they serve looks like from here. Nothing is installed or enabled; applying it is still a separate step.

data.name: ModLists_MakeCopyToolTip
data.value: Imported lists are read-only. This starts your own copy of it.

data.name: ModLists_StopFollowingToolTip
data.value: Clears which list this install is following. Nothing on disk changes.

data.name: ModLists_DeleteToolTip
data.value: Removes the list. Nothing on disk changes.

data.name: ModLists_AddModsToolTip
data.value: Put mods on this list - ones you have installed, or ones from sp-mod.com you haven't. Nothing is downloaded.

data.name: ModLists_RefreshVersionsToolTip
data.value: Reads the version of every mod on this list that is installed here, and updates the list to match. Scope is left alone, and mods you don't have are left as written. Nothing is downloaded or installed - Save keeps the changes.

data.name: ModLists_SaveToolTip
data.value: Write these changes to the list. Nothing is installed, enabled or disabled - Apply does that.

data.name: ModLists_DiscardToolTip
data.value: Throw these changes away and show the list as it is saved.

data.name: ModLists_PublishToolTip
data.value: Writes this list into the Server Map mod's config folder on this machine, so the server serves it to connected clients. Nothing is installed or changed on disk.

data.name: ModLists_ImportedNotice
data.value: This list came from someone else, so it stays exactly as they wrote it. Make a copy to change what's on it.

data.name: ModLists_UnsavedFormat
data.value: {0} - save the list to keep them. Then Preview and Apply to use the saved version.
data.comment: {0} is a count of unsaved changes, composed in the view model. One key rather than a label beside a sentence: the two halves are one sentence and cannot be reordered separately.

data.name: ModLists_EntrySearchToolTip
data.value: Matches the mod's name, the name the list stored, and the folders it installs into.

data.name: ModLists_ScopeFilterToolTip
data.value: Show only the entries meant for one kind of machine. Server only are the mods a player is never asked to install; Client only are the ones a Fika headless client skips.

data.name: ModLists_EntrySortToolTip
data.value: Ordered by the name shown on the row.

data.name: ModLists_NoEntries
data.value: This list names no mods yet. Add some, or capture what you have installed as a new list.

data.name: ModLists_NoMatches
data.value: Nothing on this list matches. Everything is still here - widen the search or the scope filter to see it.

data.name: ModLists_EntryPinnedToolTip
data.value: Pinned on this install - no list you apply will set it aside

data.name: ModLists_ScopeToolTip
data.value: Which machines this entry is for - the server, playing clients, a Fika headless client, or any combination of them. Capture works this out from where the mod's files live; change it for the exceptions, like a server mod nobody playing needs to install, or a HUD mod a headless client has no use for.

data.name: ModLists_RemoveEntryToolTip
data.value: Take this mod off the list. It stays installed - nothing on disk changes.

data.name: ModLists_PinToolTip
data.value: Pin this mod so no list you apply ever sets it aside. For the HUD and quality-of-life mods you want kept whatever list you switch to. Unpin it here or from the mod on the Installed page.

data.name: ModLists_UnpinToolTip
data.value: Unpin this mod. Lists will be able to set it aside again, and this one would.

data.name: Options_InstallFolderDescription
data.value: Point this at your SPT server install folder (the one containing SPT.Server.exe). Once set, the installed SPT version is used to default the Browse version filter and to flag mods that aren't built for it.
data.comment: SPT.Server.exe is a file name and stays as it is.

data.name: Options_BrowseEllipsis
data.comment: Button that opens a folder picker.

data.name: Options_MachineRoleDescription
data.value: A Fika headless client hosts raids without anybody playing on it, so it needs the mods that decide how a raid goes - bots, items, locations - and none of the ones that draw things at a player. Saying which this machine is lets a mod list a server hands you arrive trimmed to what this machine actually needs. It never changes a list of your own, and it never affects what you can install by hand.
data.comment: Fika is a mod's name and stays as it is.

data.name: Options_PlaysHereToolTip
data.value: Turn this off for a dedicated headless box - one that hosts raids and that nobody sits at.

data.name: Options_PlaysHereOn
data.comment: Label on a switch, shown when it is on.

data.name: Options_PlaysHereOff
data.comment: Label on the same switch, shown when it is off.

data.name: Options_HeadlessToolTip
data.value: Detected from the Fika headless launcher in the install folder, and overridable here for a setup that starts its headless some other way.

data.name: Options_HeadlessOn
data.value: This machine runs a Fika headless client

data.name: Options_HeadlessOff
data.value: This machine does not run a headless client

data.name: Options_NoHeadlessLauncherNotice
data.value: No Fika headless launcher was found in the install folder, so nothing here starts one - name it below, or leave it and the switch above still decides which mods a served list brings.

data.name: Options_HeadlessLauncherDescription
data.value: Leave this empty and the app looks for FikaHeadlessManager.exe at the top of the install folder. Point it at the exe yourself if it lives anywhere else - it does not have to be inside the install folder at all. It is used as-is, and ignored if the file isn't there.
data.comment: FikaHeadlessManager.exe is a file name and stays as it is.

data.name: Options_HeadlessLauncherPlaceholder
data.comment: Placeholder in the launcher path box - it means the app will look for it.

data.name: Options_ClearHeadlessLauncherToolTip
data.value: Back to looking in the install folder.

data.name: Options_AppearanceDescription
data.value: Follow system matches Windows and keeps matching it when you change it there. Light and Dark pin the app to one regardless.
data.comment: Follow system, Light and Dark are the three entries of the dropdown below - translate them the same way there.

data.name: Options_WindowDescription
data.value: How the window opens. Remembering the last size and position is the default, since dragging the window to a size and leaving it there is already an answer. Full screen fills the whole monitor with no title bar and covers the taskbar, which maximised does not - F11 switches into and out of it at any time, whichever of these is chosen.
data.comment: F11 is a keyboard key and stays as it is.

data.name: Options_WidthPlaceholder
data.comment: Placeholder in the window width box.

data.name: Options_HeightPlaceholder
data.comment: Placeholder in the window height box.

data.name: Options_UseCurrentSizeToolTip
data.value: Fills these boxes from the window as it is right now. Restore it down from maximised first - a maximised window has no chosen size to read.

data.name: Options_PageDefaultsDescription
data.value: The Installed and Browse pages each have a Save as default button beside Clear filters. It opens that page with the filters, sort, per-page - and on Installed, the view - it is set to at the time, so a page you always narrow the same way arrives narrowed. What you have typed in the search box is never part of it. Clearing a default here puts the page back to the app's own.
data.comment: Save as default and Clear filters are the two buttons named in Common_SaveAsDefault and Common_ClearFilters - translate them the same way here.

data.name: Options_ClearInstalledDefault
data.comment: Installed is the page name, as in the sidebar.

data.name: Options_ClearBrowseDefault
data.comment: Browse is the page name, as in the sidebar.

data.name: Options_ModPagesDescription
data.value: Before anything downloads, this app asks you to open the mod's page - where its author puts install steps, requirements, known conflicts and warnings. Turn that off if you would rather go straight to installing. This app's own updates always ask, since that page is where its release notes are.

data.name: Options_ModPagesSwitchOn
data.value: Off - install without opening mod pages
data.comment: Label on the switch when it is ON. The switch turns the asking OFF, which is why the label reads the other way round.

data.name: Options_ModPagesSwitchOff
data.value: On - open each mod's page first
data.comment: Label on the same switch when it is OFF, meaning the app still asks.

data.name: Options_FootprintDescription
data.value: Adds a page that reads the files each installed mod ships and describes how much of the game it is positioned to touch, and where any cost would land - client or server, CPU, GPU, memory or start-up. Nothing on it is timed or measured: what a mod actually costs you depends on your hardware, your settings and the other mods you run, none of which it can see. A heavy footprint means a mod reaches a long way into the game, which is usually why you installed it - it is a place to start looking, not a verdict. Off by default.

data.name: Options_SidebarOn
data.comment: Label on a switch that adds a page to the sidebar. Used by both the Mod footprint and Server map switches.

data.name: Options_SidebarOff
data.comment: The same switch, off.

data.name: Options_ServerMapDescription
data.value: Adds a page that connects to an SPT server running the Server Map mod, so you can see what it runs and compare it against what you have installed. The mod goes on the server, not here - without it this page has nothing to show, which is why it is off by default. Use the same address and port you put in the SPT launcher; connecting sends nothing about your install, it only asks the server who it is.
data.comment: Server Map is the mod's name and stays as it is.

data.name: Options_ServerMapModNotice
data.value: Running a server? The Server Map mod is a separate download - get it from the mod's page and install it on the machine running SPT. Players joining that server need nothing but this switch.

data.name: Options_GetServerMapModToolTip
data.value: Opens the Server Map mod's page on sp-mod.com in your browser.

data.name: Options_ServerAddressPlaceholder
data.comment: 127.0.0.1 is an address and stays as it is.

data.name: Options_SharedKeyPlaceholder
data.value: Shared key (if the server needs one)

data.name: Options_GenerateKeyToolTip
data.value: Replaces this server's key with a new one. Everyone using the old key stops being able to see what this server publishes until you send them the new one. The server picks it up without being restarted.

data.name: Options_ForgetCertificateToolTip
data.value: Clears the recorded fingerprint. The next connection records whatever the server presents, the same as the first one did.

data.name: Options_DataFilesDescription
data.value: View or hand-edit the JSON files this app keeps under Data\, including installed-mods.json - useful when the Installed page's own version controls aren't enough.
data.comment: Data\ and installed-mods.json are a folder and a file name - leave both exactly as they are.

data.name: Common_Cancel
data.comment: Dismisses a confirmation on the Play page, and cancels a download on the Downloads page.

data.name: ModUpdate_CurrentlyInstalledFormat
data.comment: {0} is a version number, or the Common_Unknown word when the app cannot tell.

data.name: ModUpdate_DowngradeToolTip
data.value: Install this older version in place of the one you have. Asks first - an older build may not read config or profile data the newer one wrote.

data.name: ModUpdate_MarkUpToDateToolTip
data.value: Record the newest published version as installed, without downloading anything

data.name: ModUpdate_ConfirmAsInstalledToolTip
data.value: Record the version selected below as installed, without downloading anything

data.name: ModUpdate_ClearOverrideToolTip
data.value: Go back to auto-detecting this mod's version from the files on disk

data.name: ModUpdate_Set
data.comment: Button beside the manual version box - records what was typed.

data.name: ModUpdate_ManualVersionPlaceholder
data.comment: 1.4.2 is an example version number.

data.name: ModUpdate_ShowAllToolTip
data.value: Include versions built for other SPT releases. They are hidden by default because you cannot use them on the SPT version you have.

data.name: ModUpdate_PublishedFormat
data.comment: {0} is a date, or the Common_Unknown word. Keep the :d - it prints the date the way the user's regional setting does.

data.name: ModUpdate_BadgeLatest
data.comment: Badge on the newest published version. Short: it sits in a small chip.

data.name: ModUpdate_BadgeInstalled
data.comment: Badge on the version currently on disk.

data.name: ModUpdate_TargetsSptFormat
data.comment: {0} is an SPT version or range, e.g. "3.10.x".

data.name: Play_ServerDescription
data.value: Starts this install's server and leaves it running in its own console window. It keeps running if you close this app. Restart stops it and starts it again - for a config edited or a server mod dropped in - and nothing here will stop it for good; close its window when you're done.
data.comment: Restart is the button named in Play_Restart - translate it the same way.

data.name: Play_Restart
data.comment: One button label used twice on this page: restarting the server, and restarting the headless launcher.

data.name: Play_RestartServerToolTip
data.value: Stops this install's server and starts it again. Only this install's - a second SPT server on another folder is left alone.

data.name: Play_RestartServerWarning
data.value: Restarting the server ends any raid running on it. Anyone in one is dropped.

data.name: Play_RestartServerConfirm
data.comment: Confirms the warning above it.

data.name: Play_LauncherDescription
data.value: Opens SPT.Launcher.exe, where you pick a profile and start the game. Start the server first - the launcher has nothing to log in to without it.
data.comment: SPT.Launcher.exe is a file name and stays as it is.

data.name: Play_HeadlessHeader
data.comment: Fika is a mod's name and stays as it is.

data.name: Play_HeadlessDescription
data.value: This install has a Fika headless launcher, which only appears on a setup running a headless client. It hosts raids for other players rather than being the one you play on - start the server first, same as the game launcher.

data.name: Play_RestartHeadlessToolTip
data.value: Stops the headless launcher and starts it again. It does not touch the server, and it does not close a game the launcher had already started.

data.name: Play_RestartHeadlessWarning
data.value: Restarting the headless ends any raid it is hosting. The server is left running, and a game this launcher already started is left alone - close that yourself if it needs to go too.

data.name: Configs_NoMatches
data.value: Nothing matches. Note that plenty of plugins only write a config the first time the game runs.

data.name: Configs_EmptyState
data.value: Pick a config file on the left to edit it.

data.name: Configs_ShowInExplorerToolTip
data.comment: Explorer is the Windows file manager - use whatever Windows calls it in your language.

data.name: Configs_UpdatePolicyLabel
data.comment: Label to the left of a dropdown.

data.name: Configs_UpdatePolicyToolTip
data.value: Applies to every config file of this mod, and is remembered in Data\mod_configs.json.
data.comment: Data\mod_configs.json is a file name - leave it exactly as it is.

data.name: Configs_AuthoredFilesToolTip
data.value: A folder inside this mod holding files you wrote - presets, for instance. An update leaves it exactly as it is, and removing the mod keeps it.

data.name: Configs_SettingsElsewhereToolTip
data.value: A settings file this mod keeps somewhere nothing would look for one, so updates carry your changes into it.

data.name: Configs_NotAConfigToolTip
data.value: Stop treating the open file as one of this mod's configs - for data that happens to sit in a folder called config.
data.comment: The folder is literally named "config" on disk - that word is a folder name here, not a description.

data.name: Configs_RevertToolTip
data.value: Put back what's on disk, discarding your changes

data.name: Downloads_RetryFailed

data.name: InstallRole_Explanation
data.value: A headless client hosts raids without anybody playing on it, so it needs the mods that decide how a raid goes - bots, items, locations - and none of the ones that draw things at a player. Knowing which this machine is lets a server's mod list arrive trimmed to what it actually needs.

That arrives with a later version of the server mod, and asks before it reports anything about this machine.

data.name: Footprint_SortByLabel

data.name: Footprint_WhatThisReadsBody
data.value: Each mod is read from the files it installs - how much of the game it patches, what it declares that the engine would call on a timer, and what it puts on disk. It describes what a mod contains, not what happens when you play: nothing here is timed or measured, and the app cannot see whether a declared component is ever created or whether a patch sits on something the game calls often. So these are counts, not a rating - this app has no way of knowing what any of it costs you, and deliberately does not grade anyone's work. Open a mod to see what was found and the limit of what each finding establishes.

data.name: Configs_DisclaimerMessage
data.value: Changing a mod's configuration can break the mod, or your game. That is not the mod author's responsibility to put right, so only change settings you understand - and say so when reporting a bug if you have edited a config. Every file is copied into Data\config-backups before it is saved.

data.name: AppUpdate_InfoMessage

As with any other mod, the page is opened before anything is downloaded so that you can read the update - no processes are circumvented as required by sp-mod.com and its authors.

data.comment: {2} is two or more. These two become one plural key in S5.

data.name: ServerMap_ListSavedOneFormat
data.value: "{0}" (revision {1}, 1 mod) is saved in your mod lists. Applying it is done from the Mod lists page, which shows what would change first.

data.name: ServerMap_ListSavedManyFormat
data.value: "{0}" (revision {1}, {2} mods) is saved in your mod lists. Applying it is done from the Mod lists page, which shows what would change first.

data.name: ServerMap_NoListHeldFormat
data.value: This server isn't publishing a mod list. "{0}" is still in your mod lists as you last fetched it - though if you were expecting to see it here, check the address is the server you published it to, and that the file reached that server's config folder.
data.comment: {0} is a list name.

data.name: ServerMap_NoList
data.value: This server doesn't publish a mod list. Its operator publishes one with "Publish to this server" on the Mod lists page, from the app on the machine running the server.
data.comment: "Publish to this server" is the button named in ModLists_Publish - translate it the same way.

data.name: ServerMap_KeyRequired
data.value: This server needs a shared key before it will send its list. Ask whoever runs it for the key and put it in the box above - they'll find it in the mod's config folder, in servermap-key.txt.
data.comment: servermap-key.txt is a file name and stays as it is.

data.name: ServerMap_KeyRejected
data.value: The server didn't accept the key. Check it against the one whoever runs the server has - it may have been re-generated since they sent it to you. Dashes and capitals don't matter.

data.name: ServerMap_ListUnreadableFormat
data.value: The server sent a list this app couldn't read - {0}.
data.comment: {0} is a parse error, which is not translated.

data.name: ServerMap_ListFetchDropped
data.value: The server answered the first time and then stopped, so the list wasn't fetched.

data.name: ServerMap_ListCertificateRejected
data.value: The list wasn't fetched - the server's certificate is not the one this app recorded.

data.name: ServerMap_ListFailedReasonFormat
data.comment: {0} is the reason, which arrives in the system's language.

data.name: ServerMap_KeyNeeded
data.value: This server needs a key. Whoever runs it will find it in the Server Map mod's config folder, in servermap-key.txt.

data.name: ServerMap_KeyOptional
data.value: Only needed if the server asks for one. It's generated by the server, not chosen - it says you were told about that server, and nothing more.

data.name: ServerMap_KeyHeld
data.value: Sent with every request except the first handshake. It identifies nobody and protects nothing on its own, so it isn't a password - don't reuse one anywhere else.

data.name: ServerMap_PublishesNothing
data.value: This server doesn't publish a mod list.

data.name: ServerMap_PublishedNamedFormat
data.comment: {0} is a list name, {1} a revision number or the Common_Unknown word.

data.name: ServerMap_PublishedNamedManyFormat
data.comment: {2} is two or more. Becomes one plural key in S5.

data.name: ServerMap_PublishedUnnamedFormat
data.comment: Used when the server publishes a list with no name.

data.name: ServerMap_NoThumbprint
data.comment: Stands in for a certificate fingerprint that has not been recorded.

data.name: ServerMap_NoPinRecorded
data.value: No certificate recorded yet. The first time this app connects it records the one the server presents, and warns you if it ever changes.

data.name: ServerMap_PinRecordedFormat
data.value: Trusting certificate {0}. SPT's certificate is self-signed for localhost, so this fingerprint - not the name on it - is what identifies the server.
data.comment: {0} is a shortened fingerprint. localhost stays as it is.
